If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to align with downward momentum.

If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) and forecast is trending up, cap late horizon (20–30 days) at 1–3% above recent peak to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, shift mid-horizon (8–15 days) forecast downward by 1–3% to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) across 10+ days, reduce forecast by 3–7% in late horizon (20–30 days) to reflect bearish sentiment persistence.

If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and forecast is trending down, increase early horizon (1–7 days) by 1–3% to counteract sentiment-driven overcorrection.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast diverges from history, apply 1–2% smoothing correction to mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reduce volatility mismatch.
